proof_legs.method: Fresh JVM per case running StartupBoundaryProbe, whose main performs only JDK setup (temp Solr home, silent loopback peer, node properties with the literal zkHost key) before calling the real NodeConfig.loadNodeConfig. It never touches EnvUtils or any NodeConfig member beforehand. JVM class-initialization logging (-Xlog:class+init) records the ordering from the JVM itself.
proof_legs.name: leg1_initialization_ordering_at_startup_boundary

proof_legs.method: Fresh JVM per case running StartupWireProbe against a local accepting peer that records the bytes the real startup client sends on connect and never answers. The captured 49-byte stream is the ZooKeeper ConnectRequest (4-byte length 45, protocol fields, then password length 16 and readOnly). The session timeout is the 4-byte big-endian field at stream offset 16; it is the only field that differs between the two captured packets, and it carries exactly the configured values 30001 and 2000. The connection wait was measured separately as the elapsed time until loadNodeConfig failed with the startup SolrException against the silent peer.
proof_legs.name: leg2_connection_and_session_timeouts_observed

summary: Both startup-boundary evidence gaps from the round-two receipt are closed at the exact fork head 4be1ad602621d2af96565355dce3804ee4744aae. Leg 1: in fresh JVMs that never pre-initialize EnvUtils or invoke the timeout helper, the JVM's own class-init log shows NodeConfig initializing first, EnvUtils initializing inside the loadNodeConfig call, and SolrZkClient after it; both legacy settings (-DwaitForZk=1 and SOLR_WAIT_FOR_ZK=1) reached the real startup client with the expected 1 second wait, the modern property won over the legacy one (5 seconds), and solr.wait.for.zk won over waitForZk. Leg 2: the actual ConnectRequest bytes were captured at a local accepting peer; the session-timeout field carried exactly 30001 ms for the absent-property fallback and 2000 ms for the explicit 2 second override, and the connection wait against the silent peer tracked the same configured values (31184 ms and 3133 ms elapsed for the full startup call).
